scope: Read-only schema/accounting/ownership audit of current455 production; no implementation, checks, builds or workloads
verdict: Canonical EntryHistory is necessary to remove rather than postpone pending/store copies. Schema is feasible if the following accounting and ordering sites migrate coherently.

must_change.requirement: Replace visible len*sizeofEntry+visible payload summaries and prefix-byte subtraction with full retained EntryHistory backing/payload/Arc/descriptor capacity charge. Partial cuts retain complete boundary allocations. Append/trim summaries must reflect actual descriptor capacity, not assumed Vec growth. Unknown/overflow must stay conservative; metadata-only changes cannot reduce charge.

Base history, overlay tail, materialize, append, promotion and full fallback all transfer/share immutable batches; no hidden Vec tail materialization. Accepted summary describes eventual canonical view while outstanding durable base and pending overlays remain separately charged until successful publication. Plan all fallible range/capacity validation before per-group or multi-group installation; publication/uncertainty fencing unchanged.

Persist payload/effect and Core reservation/staging inspections must use new retained backing/layout charges including descriptor capacity and temporary conversions. RPC Vec costs remain Vec costs. Preserve existing raw role/shape/byte validation and singleton gates, no new unrelated fixed batch ceiling. Full-owner charge even when physically shared; never divide by Arc refcount.

Completion/replay contiguous borrow or single Cow coalescing; application sees the same complete ordered commit batch once. Reserve worst-case visible-entry Vec plus payload/config clone charge and live history backing before accepted work, not after Durable mutation. Keep following effects/error behavior and owned Committed Vec semantics. Borrowed history range iteration must not allocate just to inspect.

Equality ignores chunk segmentation/capacity; pointer equality certifies only identical immutable content/span, never different boundary offsets. Protected checkpoint comparison ranges must iterate without coalescing or traversing certified prefix. Full arbitrary GroupLog comparison remains exact. Logical-voter inspections of canonical histories must charge backing metadata/hidden entries rather than Vec-style visible entry cost.

Wire/WAL/checkpoint iteration encodes visible entries only with unchanged semantic byte formats/count/error priority. Codec capture charges new allocation layout before allocation where bounded; snapshots/recovery rebuild fresh histories. Striped payload stripping and logical-voter single-entry removal create explicit independent replacements; no mutable backing escape.

boundary_pin_rule: For each owner charge every full backing reachable from its visible spans plus descriptor allocation. Removing every span drops backing handles; partial trim cannot subtract invisible elements/payloads still pinned. Repeated trim/append/replacement must stay bounded by admitted physical allocations, not merely visible max_entries. Raw imported/recovered spare capacity and descriptor spare capacity remain observable and fully charged.
conversion_rule: Arc<Vec> capture can move the existing Vec without copying elements, but has its own checked padded allocation; empty Vec with spare capacity requires explicit raw-shape policy before normalization. IntoVec when shared and cross-chunk Cow materialization may clone configuration payloads; worst-case old+new memory must be reserved, no unbounded hidden materialization from Debug/Index/AsRef.
failure_rule: Allocation planning and validation do not move the original error gates or mutate canonical state before all fallible checks finish. Native sync+manifest remains the sole durable promotion boundary; failure/cancellation/shutdown drops only its own handles, never invalidates another owner. Restart never treats Arc identity as ticket or persisted authority.
essential_existing_schema_controls: Independent Vec oracle across chunk splits and both trim boundaries
Partial-span hidden payload plus descriptor/backing charge, overflow and spare capacity
Altered update replacement including configuration and identical header/different bytes
Core/provider retain same backing through admitted and exact Durable, with failed/stale completions
Cross-chunk application one-batch error/partial outcome and following-effect ordering
Modeled native publication/recovery and exact checkpoint lineage histories
